requirements.quote:
An alternative form of anti-replay is to record a unique value
   derived from the ClientHello (generally either the random value or
   the PSK binder) and reject duplicates.
requirements.condition: when implementing the ClientHello-recording anti-replay mechanism
requirements.required_behavior: record a unique value derived from each ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The replay-cache insertion key can be traced to the received ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
An alternative form of anti-replay is to record a unique value
   derived from the ClientHello (generally either the random value or
   the PSK binder) and reject duplicates.
requirements.condition: when the ClientHello-recording mechanism sees a duplicate recorded value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat the duplicate as a fresh 0-RTT ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The same ClientHello-derived key can be submitted twice and the second 0-RTT decision observed.

requirements.quote:
In order to implement this, when a ClientHello is received, the
   server first verifies the PSK binder as described in Section 4.2.11.
requirements.condition: when a server using ClientHello recording receives a ClientHello that offers a PSK
requirements.required_behavior: verify the PSK binder before proceeding with replay-cache processing
requirements.forbidden_behavior: derive replay-cache state from the ClientHello before verifying the selected PSK binder
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation or a malformed binder can verify ordering between binder validation and replay-cache access.

requirements.quote:
It then computes the expected_arrival_time as described in the next
   section and rejects 0-RTT if it is outside the recording window,
   falling back to the 1-RTT handshake.
requirements.condition: after PSK-binder verification in the ClientHello-recording mechanism
requirements.why_checkable: The server's freshness calculation can be exercised with controlled ticket ages and clock values.

requirements.quote:
It then computes the expected_arrival_time as described in the next
   section and rejects 0-RTT if it is outside the recording window,
   falling back to the 1-RTT handshake.
requirements.condition: when expected_arrival_time is outside the ClientHello recording window
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept early data for that ClientHello
requirements.error_behavior: reject 0-RTT without requiring termination of the connection
requirements.why_checkable: A ticket age outside the configured recording window can verify the early-data rejection path.

requirements.quote:
It then computes the expected_arrival_time as described in the next
   section and rejects 0-RTT if it is outside the recording window,
   falling back to the 1-RTT handshake.
requirements.condition: when expected_arrival_time is outside the ClientHello recording window
requirements.error_behavior: continue using the 1-RTT handshake path after rejecting 0-RTT
requirements.why_checkable: The handshake can be observed to continue without early-data acceptance after the freshness failure.

requirements.quote:
If the expected_arrival_time is in the window, then the server checks
   to see if it has recorded a matching ClientHello.
requirements.condition: when expected_arrival_time is inside the recording window
requirements.required_behavior: check the recording store for a matching ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept 0-RTT without consulting the recording store
requirements.why_checkable: Replay-store lookup can be instrumented or inferred from decisions for pre-populated matching entries.

requirements.quote:
If one is found,
   it either aborts the handshake with an "illegal_parameter" alert or
   accepts the PSK but rejects 0-RTT.
requirements.condition: when a matching ClientHello is already recorded
requirements.error_behavior: do not accept early data for the replay
requirements.why_checkable: A replay-cache hit can verify that the server never accepts 0-RTT for the recorded ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
If one is found,
   it either aborts the handshake with an "illegal_parameter" alert or
   accepts the PSK but rejects 0-RTT.
requirements.condition: when a matching ClientHello is already recorded and the server chooses to abort
requirements.why_checkable: The alert emitted on the replay-cache-hit abort path can be captured and compared with illegal_parameter.

requirements.quote:
If one is found,
   it either aborts the handshake with an "illegal_parameter" alert or
   accepts the PSK but rejects 0-RTT.
requirements.condition: when a matching ClientHello is already recorded and the server does not abort
requirements.required_behavior: accept the PSK for the continuing non-0-RTT handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A replay-cache hit on the non-abort path can verify PSK resumption continues while early data remains rejected.

requirements.quote:
If no matching ClientHello is
   found, then it accepts 0-RTT and then stores the ClientHello for as
   long as the expected_arrival_time is inside the window.
requirements.condition: when expected_arrival_time is inside the recording window and no matching ClientHello is recorded
requirements.why_checkable: A fresh in-window ClientHello can verify the early-data acceptance decision.

requirements.quote:
If no matching ClientHello is
   found, then it accepts 0-RTT and then stores the ClientHello for as
   long as the expected_arrival_time is inside the window.
requirements.condition: after accepting 0-RTT for a fresh in-window ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: store the ClientHello while its expected_arrival_time remains inside the recording window
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit the recording needed to detect another in-window use
requirements.why_checkable: A second presentation during the window can verify that the first acceptance created retained replay state.

requirements.quote:
Servers MAY
   also implement data stores with false positives, such as Bloom
   filters, in which case they MUST respond to apparent replay by
   rejecting 0-RTT but MUST NOT abort the handshake.
requirements.condition: when a false-positive-capable replay store reports an apparent replay
requirements.error_behavior: reject early data without aborting the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A forced false-positive lookup can verify that early data is rejected.

requirements.quote:
Servers MAY
   also implement data stores with false positives, such as Bloom
   filters, in which case they MUST respond to apparent replay by
   rejecting 0-RTT but MUST NOT abort the handshake.
requirements.condition: when a false-positive-capable replay store reports an apparent replay
requirements.forbidden_behavior: abort the handshake because of the apparent replay
requirements.error_behavior: reject 0-RTT but do not abort the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A forced false positive can verify that the connection remains on a non-0-RTT handshake path.

requirements.quote:
The server MUST derive the storage key only from validated sections
   of the ClientHello.
requirements.condition: when deriving the ClientHello replay-storage key
requirements.required_behavior: derive the key exclusively from validated ClientHello sections
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include any unvalidated ClientHello section in the storage key
requirements.why_checkable: Mutating an unvalidated binder or extension can verify that it does not alter replay-cache identity.

requirements.quote:
In this case, the best anti-replay protection
   is provided by having a single storage zone be authoritative for a
   given ticket and refusing 0-RTT for that ticket in any other zone.
requirements.condition: when a distributed system cannot maintain globally consistent storage of received ClientHellos
requirements.required_behavior: designate one storage zone as authoritative for each ticket
requirements.why_checkable: Ticket routing and replay-cache ownership can be inspected to verify a single authoritative zone.

requirements.quote:
In this case, the best anti-replay protection
   is provided by having a single storage zone be authoritative for a
   given ticket and refusing 0-RTT for that ticket in any other zone.
requirements.condition: when a ticket is presented for 0-RTT outside its authoritative storage zone
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept 0-RTT for the ticket in a non-authoritative zone
requirements.why_checkable: The same ticket can be routed to each zone and the 0-RTT decision observed.

requirements.quote:
When implementations are freshly started, they SHOULD reject 0-RTT as
   long as any portion of their recording window overlaps the startup
   time.
requirements.condition: after startup while any portion of the recording window overlaps the startup time
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept 0-RTT during the overlapping startup interval
requirements.error_behavior: reject early data until the recording window no longer overlaps startup
requirements.why_checkable: Controlled startup time and ticket ages can verify the early-data decision across the overlap boundary.
